vocab.title: Build your word bank
vocab.levelLabel: Choose JLPT level for vocabulary examples:
vocab.description: Learn new words with their hiragana reading, romaji, and meaning. Each card includes an example sentence so you see the word in context.

kanji.title: Master the characters
kanji.levelLabel: Choose JLPT level for kanji examples:
kanji.description: Each kanji is presented with its on'yomi (Chinese reading), kun'yomi (Japanese reading), core meaning, and JLPT level — everything you need in one glance.

grammar.title: Learn sentence patterns
grammar.levelLabel: Choose JLPT level for grammar examples:
grammar.description: Grammar in Sukuro is taught through practical patterns. Each lesson shows the structure, explains the usage, and provides a real example sentence with translation.

p1.label: Basic assertion
p1.explanation: States a fact or describes something. The most fundamental sentence structure in Japanese.

p2.label: Ongoing action
p2.explanation: Expresses an action in progress or a continuing state at the moment of speaking.

p3.label: Expressing likes
p3.explanation: Used to express that you like or are fond of something or someone.

kana.title: Learn hiragana and katakana
kana.description: Sukuro also helps you build a strong reading foundation with both Japanese syllabaries.

hiragana.title: Hiragana
hiragana.description: Used for native Japanese words and grammar endings.

katakana.title: Katakana
katakana.description: Used mainly for foreign words, names, and emphasis.

jlpt.title: Choose your favorite JLPT level
jlpt.description: You can focus your learning on the JLPT level that matches your objective, from beginner to advanced.

n5.label: Beginner
n5.description: Focuses on basic vocabulary, essential kanji, and simple sentence patterns for daily conversation.

n4.label: Elementary
n4.description: Introduces more grammar and vocabulary to understand common situations and short passages.

n3.label: Intermediate
n3.description: Covers more nuanced grammar and broader vocabulary used in real conversations and media.

n2.label: Upper-intermediate
n2.description: Targets advanced reading/listening comprehension for news, formal contexts, and complex topics.

n1.label: Advanced
n1.description: Emphasizes subtle grammar, abstract topics, and high-level comprehension close to native usage.

g1.label: Basic assertion
g1.explanation: States a fact or describes something in the simplest form.

g2.label: Expressing likes
g2.explanation: Used to express what you like.

g1.label: Obligation
g1.explanation: Expresses that something must be done.
g1.translation: I must practice kanji every day.

g2.label: Opinion
g2.translation: I think this grammar is important.

g1.label: Purpose / Wish
g1.explanation: Indicates purpose or a desired outcome.
g1.translation: I practice so that I can speak Japanese.

g2.label: Established rule
g2.explanation: Shows a rule, schedule, or arrangement already decided.
g2.translation: In class, we are supposed to use only Japanese.

g1.label: No more than
g1.explanation: Emphasizes that something is merely / only.
g1.translation: This is nothing more than one example.

g2.label: Along with
g2.explanation: Indicates that one change accompanies another.
g2.translation: As your level improves, your vocabulary also grows.

g1.label: Concerning / over
g1.explanation: Used for debates or issues surrounding a topic.

g2.label: Cannot help but
g2.explanation: Expresses an irresistible feeling or reaction.
g2.translation: I cannot help but be surprised hearing this story.

ai.title: Powered by AI
ai.description: Tap the AI button on any flashcard to get a clear, context-aware explanation generated by Google Gemini — directly inside the app, no extra searching needed.
ai.s1Body: 曖昧 (aimai) refers to something vague, ambiguous, or lacking clarity. It can describe an answer, a feeling, a rule, or a situation that is not clearly defined. The kanji 曖 carries the nuance of something dim or hidden, while 昧 evokes obscurity — together they paint a picture of intentional or accidental vagueness.
ai.s2Body: 曖昧 is a な-adjective, so it combines directly with nouns (曖昧な + noun) and becomes an adverb with に (曖昧に + verb). You will often encounter it in phrases like 曖昧な返事 (a vague answer), 曖昧な態度 (a non-committal attitude), or 曖昧に答える (to answer vaguely).
ai.s3Body: In Japanese communication, a direct "no" is often avoided to preserve social harmony (和, wa). 曖昧な言い方 — an ambiguous way of speaking — is therefore very common in polite or professional contexts. Learning to read these subtle, indirect signals is key to truly understanding real Japanese.

intro.title: 1. Introduction
intro.text: Welcome to Sukuro. Your privacy matters to us. This policy explains what data the app handles and how we use it. The short version: Sukuro does not collect any personal information and does not require you to create an account.

data.title: 2. Data we collect
data.text: Sukuro does not collect any personal information. No account creation, no email address, and no personal identifier is ever required or stored. The only data generated by the app is:
data.local: Learning progress (completed lessons, scores, vocabulary learned): stored exclusively on your device using local storage. It is never transmitted to our servers.
data.technical: Crash reports and anonymous usage statistics: may be collected by the Google Play Store or Apple App Store platforms. This is handled solely by those platforms under their respective privacy policies, outside of our control.

ai.title: 3. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
ai.text: Sukuro uses Google Gemini (Google Generative AI) to generate educational content such as explanations and example sentences.
ai.point1: When you request an AI explanation, the text of the relevant exercise or question is sent to Google's servers for processing. No personal information is included in these requests.
ai.point2: According to Google's standard API terms of use, this data is not used to train their models and is processed solely to generate the immediate response shown in the app.

sharing.title: 4. Third-party services
sharing.text: We do not sell, trade, or share any personal data. The only third-party service used by Sukuro is:
sharing.google: Google Gemini API: Used to generate AI-powered explanations and example sentences. Exercise text may be processed on Google's servers. Please refer to Google's Privacy Policy for details.
sharing.note: No other third-party analytics, tracking, or advertising services are used.

storage.title: 5. Data storage and deletion
storage.text: All your learning data is stored locally on your device. We do not maintain any server-side database of your personal information. To permanently delete all app data, simply uninstall Sukuro from your device.

contact.title: 6. Contact

q1.q: Is my learning progress saved if I change devices?
q1.a: Your progress is currently stored locally on your device. Switching to a new device or reinstalling the app will reset your progress. Cross-device sync may be added in a future update.

q2.q: Does Sukuro collect any personal data?
q2.a: No. Sukuro does not require an account and does not collect any personal information. Your learning progress stays on your device. The only external service used is Google Gemini for AI explanations. For full details, see our Privacy Policy.
